objective: Test whether a model-free bar-regularity check brings single-network downbeats (Beat This! minimal + D1) to two-network safety at lower cost.
current_unknown: Whether the cheaper single-network configuration can be made as safe as madmom DBN + D3.
hypothesis: C5 = C2 + R meets: silent error rate <= 0.0336, false-alarm rate <= 0.05, cost <= 9.83 CPU-s per audio-minute.
competing_hypotheses: C2's silent errors keep regular bar lengths, so R cannot see them.
R removes silent errors but floods false alarms on genuine odd bars beyond 0.05.

stages.output: Rule R, configuration C5 and decision thresholds pre-registered in commit 355eb3b.
R unit checks pass (regular grid unflagged; a short bar flags both of its bounding downbeats); suite test added.
Recomputed C2 reproduces GRID-METER-004 exactly: 40/824 silent, 0 false alarms.

stages.note: False-alarm traps (sync_anticip, halftime_switch) already inside the decision set; both produced 0 C5 false alarms.

stages.output: C5 recommended over C1: silent 0.0279 vs 0.0286, FA 0.0256, coverage 0.966 vs 0.791, cost 5.84 vs 16.38 CPU-s per audio-minute.
GRID-METER-003 should verify C5's grid; amend its method before any real track is analysed.

regression_check.compared_metric: C2 silent errors / decoded / false alarms
regression_check.detail: 40/824 silent and 0 false alarms reproduced exactly.

limitations: Synthetic fixtures only; R assumes the modal bar length is the true one.
CPU time on an x86 container core is a proxy, not a device measurement.
Remaining silent errors on steady fixtures (3-4 each) not investigated.
Repeated irregular phrases (heyya_pattern) remain unsafe: 62 silent errors.

next_recommended_experiment.reason: Real-track validation of the new candidate C5; blocked on one human input.

human_interventions: GRID-METER-003 needs real tracks and listener verification.
